scenario: 缓存集群 10 台机器按 hash(key)%N 路由，存了千万条目，现在要扩容到 11 台。
scenario_en: A ten-node cache cluster routes with hash(key) modulo N and holds tens of millions of entries, and you now add an eleventh node.
q: 用 hash(key) % N 分配服务器，增删一台服务器会发生什么？
q_en: With hash(key) modulo N server assignment, what happens when you add or remove a server?
options: N 变了，几乎所有 key 重新映射
只有新加那台服务器的数据需要迁移
什么都不会发生
数据自动均匀迁移，无成本
options_en: N changes, so almost every key maps to a different server — most data must move, a disaster at millions of entries.
Only the newly added server's data needs to migrate.
Nothing happens at all.
Data automatically migrates evenly at no cost.
why: 取模分布对 N 极度敏感；这正是一致性哈希要解决的问题。
why_en: With modulo hashing, adding or removing a server changes N so almost every key remaps and most data must move.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 key 的哈希值对服务器数 N 取余来决定归属的最简单分布方式，对 N 的变化极度敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo hashing takes a key's hash mod the server count N to decide ownership, and it's extremely sensitive to any change in N.

codeSample:
server_index = hash(key) % N
# N: 10 -> 11 remaps almost every existing key
optionExplanations: 对，取模用的是服务器总数 N，N 一变几乎每个 key 的归属都要重算。
取模没有局部性保护，牵动的不只是新机器，几乎所有旧 key 也要重新分配。
增删节点确实会触发大规模重新映射，不是悄无声息就完成的。
重新映射意味着数据要真的搬家，既不自动也不是零成本。
optionExplanations_en: Right — modulo uses the total server count N, so changing N forces almost every key to be remapped to a different server.
Modulo has no locality protection; it's not just the new machine, nearly every existing key gets reassigned too.
Adding or removing a node does trigger a large-scale remap; it doesn't pass silently.
A remap means data actually has to move across machines — that's neither automatic nor free.

scenario: 缓存集群要能随时加减节点，每次变更迁移的 key 越少越好，且不想维护中心路由表。
scenario_en: A cache cluster must add and remove nodes at any time, move as few keys as possible per change, and avoid a central routing table.
q: 一致性哈希的工作方式是？
q_en: How does consistent hashing work?
options: 按 key 首字母分配服务器
维护一张全局路由表
服务器和 key 哈希到虚拟环上
每次请求广播到所有节点
options_en: Assign servers by a key's first letter.
Maintain one global routing table.
Both servers and keys hash onto a virtual ring, and a key belongs to the next server found clockwise; adding a node only moves the keys between it and its neighbor.
Broadcast every request to all nodes.
why: 环结构把增删节点的影响局部化：移除节点时也只有它的 key 迁给环上的下一台。Memcached/Redis Cluster、Cassandra/DynamoDB、部分 LB 和 CDN 都在用。
why_en: Consistent hashing places servers and keys on a ring where each key belongs to the next server clockwise, so only a small range moves when nodes change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希里承载服务器和 key 哈希值的环形结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The virtual ring is the circular structure that holds the hashed positions of servers and keys in consistent hashing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一张查找表记录每条数据在哪个分片的方式，灵活但每次请求多一跳依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table to record which shard holds each item, flexible but adding an extra hop of dependency per request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的分布式内存缓存系统，常用一致性哈希分布 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memcached is a common distributed in-memory cache that often uses consistent hashing to distribute keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 宽列分布式数据库，用一致性哈希做分片，强调高写入吞吐和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column distributed database that uses consistent hashing for sharding and emphasizes high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on edge servers close to users.

optionExplanations: 按首字母切分只在玩具例子里均匀，现实 key 分布很容易严重倾斜。
维护全局路由表是目录式分片的做法，每次路由都要多查一次表。
对，服务器和 key 都映射进同一个环，顺时针找下一台，增删节点只影响相邻一小段。
广播能做发现或同步元数据，但定位单条数据归属不需要问遍全部节点。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting by first letter only looks even in toy examples; real key distributions skew badly.
Maintaining a global routing table is what directory-based sharding does, adding a lookup hop per request.
Right — servers and keys both hash onto one ring, each key belongs to the next server clockwise, so add/remove only touches a small local range.
Broadcasting can discover nodes or sync metadata, but locating one key's owner doesn't need asking every node.

scenario: 线上缓存/分片集群要弹性伸缩，纠结该用简单取模还是一致性哈希分配节点。
scenario_en: An online cache or shard cluster needs elastic scaling, and you are choosing modulo hashing or consistent hashing.
q: 10 台服务器的集群加 1 台：简单取模 vs 一致性哈希，各要移动多少数据？
q_en: In a 10-server cluster adding one server, how much data moves with modulo hashing versus consistent hashing?
options: 都是 50%
取模 ~90% vs 一致性哈希 ~10%
取模 ~10% vs 一致性哈希 ~90%
都不用移动
options_en: Both about fifty percent.
About ninety percent with modulo versus about ten percent with consistent hashing.
About ten percent with modulo versus about ninety percent with consistent hashing.
Neither needs to move any data.
why: 这组数字就是一致性哈希的价值：动态增删节点不再引发海量数据迁移，这个比例直接决定了扩缩容操作是否安全、可以随时做。
why_en: Adding one server to ten means moving about ninety percent of data with modulo hashing but only about ten percent with consistent hashing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 key 的哈希值对服务器数 N 取余来决定归属的最简单分布方式，对 N 的变化极度敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo hashing takes a key's hash mod the server count N to decide ownership, and it's extremely sensitive to any change in N.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

codeSample:
# modulo: nearly all keys remap when N changes
server = hash(key) % N

# consistent hashing: only the range between the
# new node and its neighbor on the ring moves
optionExplanations: 50/50 掩盖了两种算法的真实差距，取模的迁移量远比一致性哈希高。
对，取模几乎重算全部映射；一致性哈希只挪相邻一小段，差距接近一个数量级。
把两种算法的迁移量说反了，一致性哈希才是省搬迁的那一个。
增删节点必然牵动数据归属，不可能完全零迁移。
optionExplanations_en: A flat fifty-fifty split hides the real gap — modulo moves far more data than consistent hashing.
Right — modulo remaps almost everything, while consistent hashing only shifts a small neighboring range, nearly an order of magnitude apart.
This swaps the two algorithms' migration costs — consistent hashing is the one that moves far less.
Adding or removing a node always shifts some keys; zero migration isn't realistic.

scenario: 面试中讨论分布式缓存的弹性扩缩容：要按负载动态加减缓存节点或数据库分片。
scenario_en: In an interview about distributed cache scaling, nodes or shards may be added and removed based on load.
q: 关于一致性哈希，说到什么程度合适？
q_en: How much detail should you give about consistent hashing in an interview?
options: 现场手推环算法的数学证明
完全不提
点到为止，除非追问才展开
背诵虚拟节点的实现代码
options_en: Derive the ring algorithm's math proof on the spot.
Don't mention it at all.
Say just enough: "we'll use consistent hashing to distribute data across nodes so scaling doesn't trigger massive data migration," and expand only if asked.
Recite the virtual-node implementation code from memory.
why: 考官通常只想确认你知道这项技术；弹性伸缩场景点名它的作用即可，别自己展开长篇原理。
why_en: In interviews just say you will use consistent hashing to distribute data across nodes; explain the internals only if asked.
whenOtherWins: 若考官明确追问工作原理，再讲环、顺时针归属和局部迁移这套机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

tradeoff: 点到为止展示知识面 vs 深入原理占用宝贵面试时间
optionExplanations: 现场推数学证明会把有限的面试时间全耗在一个细节上，考官也不需要证明。
完全不提会让考官看不出你知道这项应对弹性伸缩的技术。
对，点名「用一致性哈希分散节点」就够，考官追问再展开原理。
背代码不是重点，考官想看的是你知不知道这个技术解决了什么问题。
optionExplanations_en: Deriving the math proof on the spot burns your limited interview time on one detail the interviewer isn't asking for.
Saying nothing at all leaves the interviewer unsure whether you know this technique exists for elastic scaling.
Right — naming 'we'll use consistent hashing to distribute nodes' is enough; expand only if asked.
Reciting implementation code misses the point — the interviewer wants to know you understand what problem it solves.

scenario: 数据库跨两个机房部署，机房间专线每月会断几十秒，你要向面试官准确表述 CAP。
scenario_en: A database spans two data centers whose link drops for tens of seconds each month, and you must state CAP precisely to the interviewer.
q: CAP 定理的准确表述是？
q_en: What is the accurate statement of the CAP theorem?
options: 三个都能同时拿到
只能同时满足两个；实际是 C vs A
CAP 只描述强一致系统，不适用于最终一致系统
只适用于单机数据库
options_en: All three can be had at once.

You can satisfy only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once; since partitions are unavoidable in distributed systems, the real choice is between consistency and availability.
CAP only describes strongly consistent systems, not eventually consistent ones.
It only applies to single-machine databases.
why: C = 所有节点看到相同数据，A = 每个请求都有响应，P = 网络断裂时系统仍工作；P 是前提，真正的选择题是 C vs A。
why_en: CAP says you can have only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance, and since partitions are unavoidable you really choose between consistency and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络连接在节点间断开时系统仍要能工作的要求，在分布式系统里几乎不可避免要满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partition tolerance requires the system to keep working even when network links between nodes fail, and in practice it's unavoidable.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["Partition happens"] --> Choice{"Choose?"}
    Choice --> C["Consistency: reject stale"]
    Choice --> A["Availability: serve stale"]
optionExplanations: 分布式系统里三者不可能同时全拿到，网络分区一发生就得取舍。
对，分区在分布式系统里几乎不可避免，真正要选的是一致性还是可用性。
CAP 讨论的是分区场景本身，不限定某一种具体的一致性模型。
单机系统不面对网络分区，CAP 讨论的正是多机分布式场景。
optionExplanations_en: In a distributed system you can't hold all three at once; a partition forces a real choice.
Right — partitions are practically unavoidable in distributed systems, so the real choice is consistency versus availability.
CAP is about partition scenarios generally, it isn't scoped to one particular consistency model.
Single-node systems don't face network partitions; CAP is specifically about multi-node distributed systems.

scenario: 支付账本和社交点赞数跑在两套系统上，机房间链路断了 30 秒。
scenario_en: A payment ledger and a social like-counter run on separate systems, and the link between data centers is down for 30 seconds.
q: 网络分区发生时，「选一致性」和「选可用性」的系统各自表现为？
q_en: During a network partition, how do consistency-first and availability-first systems behave?
options: 两者都直接宕机
两者都继续服务且数据一致
选 C 的系统所有节点数据分歧；选 A 的系统拒绝请求
选 C 拒绝服务；选 A 继续响应会分歧
options_en: Both go straight down.
Both keep serving with consistent data.
A consistency-first system has diverging data on every node; an availability-first system refuses requests.

Consistency-first: some nodes refuse to serve rather than risk returning stale data; availability-first: every node keeps responding, data may diverge temporarily, and it converges once the partition heals.
why: 选 C = 宁可拒绝服务也要数据正确；选 A = 宁可短暂不一致也要有响应。这是分区期间的行为差异。
why_en: A consistency-first system refuses requests rather than serve stale data during a partition, while an availability-first system keeps responding and converges later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。

tradeoff: 拒绝请求保正确 vs 继续响应容忍分歧
optionExplanations: 分区时两边至少有一边还在响应，不会同时直接宕机。
分区期间不可能既保证全部一致又保证每个请求都成功，这两个目标互斥。
把 C 和 A 各自的行为说反了，照这个理解后续取舍会全错。
对，C 宁可拒绝部分请求也不给旧数据；A 继续响应，数据可能短暂分歧。
optionExplanations_en: During a partition at least one side keeps responding; they don't both just go dark.
During a partition you can't have every node consistent and every request succeed at the same time — the two goals conflict.
This swaps C and A's actual behaviors, which would send every later tradeoff call the wrong way.
Right — C would rather refuse some requests than serve stale data, while A keeps answering and may briefly diverge.

scenario: 设计社交 feed、推荐系统或分析仪表盘，被问一致性模型怎么选。
scenario_en: You are designing a social feed, recommendation system, or analytics dashboard and need to choose a consistency model.
q: 安全的默认答案是？
q_en: What is the safer default consistency answer for feeds, recommendations, or analytics?
options: 可用性优先，最终一致
全系统强一致
弱一致，不保证收敛
线性一致
options_en: Availability-first with eventual consistency — users tolerate a feed that's two seconds stale, but not an app that won't open.
Strong consistency across the whole system.
Weak consistency, with no convergence guarantee.
Linearizable consistency.
why: 大多数系统默认选可用性：最终一致保证「无新更新时所有节点终将收敛」，对 feed/推荐/分析完全够用。
why_en: For most systems availability is the right default: users tolerate a slightly stale feed but not a down app, so eventual consistency works.
whenOtherWins: 题目一旦涉及钱、库存、订限量资源（订座），就要切到强一致。

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。

termDefinitions.meaning: 不承诺节点数据会收敛、也不保证顺序的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weak consistency makes no guarantee that replicas will ever converge or that updates are seen in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最严格的一致性模型，所有操作看起来像按一个全局顺序瞬时发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability is the strictest consistency model, making all operations appear to happen instantly in one global order.

tradeoff: 可用性默认（最终一致） vs 强一致带来的协调延迟
optionExplanations: 对，用户能忍 feed 慢几秒，但忍不了打不开的 App，最终一致对这些场景够用。
全系统都上强一致会付出协调延迟和可用性下降的代价，feed/推荐用不上这么重。
弱一致连收敛都不承诺，展示型数据也很难接受这么松的保证。
线性一致是最严格的模型，代价最高，留给真的需要防超卖的路径。
optionExplanations_en: Right — users tolerate a feed that's a few seconds stale far more than an app that won't load, so eventual consistency is enough here.
Strong consistency everywhere pays a coordination-latency and availability cost that feeds or recommendations don't need.
Weak consistency doesn't even promise convergence, which is too loose even for display-only data.
Linearizability is the strictest, costliest model, best reserved for paths that truly must prevent overselling.

scenario: 库存计数、银行账户余额、Ticketmaster 座位预订——读到几秒前的旧数据就会超卖 / 放过欺诈 / 重复订座。
scenario_en: Inventory counts, bank balances, or ticket seats can oversell, allow fraud, or double-book if reads are stale by a few seconds.
q: 一致性模型该选？
q_en: Which consistency model should you choose for stale-read-sensitive paths?
options: 最终一致
弱一致
强一致（防超卖）
不需要一致性
options_en: Eventual consistency.
Weak consistency.
Strong consistency, because stale data causes real financial loss.
No consistency guarantee needed.
why: 强一致的适用判据是「陈旧读会造成实际业务损失」；同一应用可混用：电商的商品描述/评论最终一致、库存/下单强一致。
why_en: Choose strong consistency when stale reads cause real business harm, like overselling inventory, fraud, or double-booked seats.
whenOtherWins: 同系统里的展示型数据（描述、评论晚 5 秒出现没人在乎）继续用最终一致即可。

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求所有节点在任意时刻看到相同、最新数据的一致性模型，代价是延迟或可用性下降。

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

tradeoff: 数据实时正确（防超卖/防欺诈） vs 协调延迟和可用性下降
optionExplanations: 最终一致允许短暂旧读，库存/余额场景陈旧几秒就可能超卖或错扣钱。
弱一致连收敛都不保证，对这类会造成实际损失的路径风险更大。
对，读到几秒前的旧数据会超卖、放过欺诈、重复订座，这类路径必须强一致。
库存、余额、订座这类共享可变状态离不开一致性保证，不可能不管。
optionExplanations_en: Eventual consistency allows brief stale reads, and a few stale seconds on inventory or balance can already cause overselling or a wrong charge.
Weak consistency doesn't even guarantee convergence, which is riskier still on paths where staleness causes real loss.
Right — reading a few-seconds-old value here can oversell inventory, miss fraud, or double-book a seat, so these paths need strong consistency.
Shared mutable state like inventory, balances, or seat bookings can't skip a consistency guarantee altogether.

scenario: 面试官问：DynamoDB 的 eventually consistent 读到底承诺了什么，能不能直接叫弱一致？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what an eventually consistent DynamoDB read actually promises, and whether you can just call it weak consistency.
q: 最终一致（eventual）与弱一致（weak）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between eventual consistency and weak consistency?
options: 最终一致承诺收敛；弱一致不承诺
两者其实是同义词，可以互换
弱一致更强
最终一致等于强一致
options_en: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes eventually converge to the same state; weak consistency makes no such convergence guarantee.
The two are synonyms and interchangeable.
Weak consistency is the stronger guarantee.
Eventual consistency is the same as strong consistency.
why: 「最终」是一个有内容的承诺——会收敛；弱一致什么都不承诺。面试别把两个词混用。
why_en: Eventual consistency guarantees all nodes converge given enough time without updates, while weak consistency makes no convergence guarantee at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证「没有新更新时所有节点终将收敛到同一状态」的一致性模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency guarantees that, given no new updates, all nodes will eventually converge to the same state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不承诺节点数据会收敛、也不保证顺序的一致性模型。

tradeoff: 承诺最终收敛 vs 不承诺任何收敛
optionExplanations: 对，最终一致至少承诺没有新写入后会收敛；弱一致什么都不保证。
两个词面试里混用会丢掉「会不会收敛」这个关键差别，不是同义词。
弱一致的保证比最终一致更少，不是更强的那一边。
强一致要求随时读到最新写入，比最终一致的收敛承诺严格得多。
optionExplanations_en: Right — eventual consistency at least promises convergence once new writes stop; weak consistency promises nothing.
Conflating the two terms in an interview loses the key difference of whether convergence is guaranteed at all.
Weak consistency actually guarantees less than eventual, not more.
Strong consistency requires reading the latest write at all times, a much stricter bar than eventual's convergence promise.

scenario: 多副本数据库全年 99.9% 时间网络正常，但跨区强一致写仍要 80ms，团队想知道 CAP 怎么解释。
scenario_en: A replicated database has healthy networks 99.9% of the year, yet a strongly consistent cross-region write still costs 80ms, and the team asks how CAP explains that.
q: PACELC 定理补充了 CAP 的什么盲区？
q_en: What blind spot in CAP does PACELC cover?
options: 网络分区发生时，PACELC 建议直接选延迟
CAP 定理其实只适用于单机部署的数据库
在实际系统里网络分区永远不会真的发生
日常运行里其实是一致性和延迟的取舍
options_en: When a partition happens, PACELC says just choose latency.
CAP theorem actually only applies to single-machine databases.
In real systems, network partitions never actually happen.
Day to day, the real tradeoff is between consistency and latency.
why: PACELC：分区（P）时选 A 或 C；否则（E）选延迟（L）或一致性（C）。日常运行中强一致的代价是协调延迟。
why_en: PACELC notes that outside rare partitions the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency, since strong consistency requires coordination before responding.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 的补充：分区时选可用性或一致性，其他时候（日常）选延迟或一致性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PACELC extends CAP: during a Partition choose Availability or Consistency, Else choose Latency or Consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容错三者在分布式系统里只能同时满足两个的定理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP theorem says a distributed system can only guarantee two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

optionExplanations: 分区时 PACELC 谈的仍是可用性还是一致性，延迟选项出现在没分区的日常运行里。
CAP 本身讨论的就是多机分布式场景，不是单机适用范围的问题。
分区当然会发生，PACELC 正是为了补上「平时」这个 CAP 没讲的部分。
对，CAP 只讲分区这种少见时刻，日常运行里真正的取舍是一致性和延迟。
optionExplanations_en: During a partition PACELC is still about availability versus consistency; latency enters the picture during normal operation.
CAP is already about multi-node distributed scenarios, not a question of single-machine scope.
Partitions certainly do happen; PACELC exists precisely to cover the everyday case CAP leaves out.
Right — CAP only covers the rare partition moment, while day to day the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency.

q: 把「订票系统选强一致」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the strong-consistency decision chain for a ticket-booking system in the right order.
steps: 选型：对这些关键路径选择强一致
需求：库存/余额/订座——读到陈旧数据会超卖、放过欺诈或重复订座
缓解：只对关键路径强一致，描述、评论等展示数据用最终一致
代价：分区时部分请求被拒，且日常延迟更高（节点需先协调）
why: 需求（陈旧读有真实代价）→ 选强一致 → 代价（可用性与延迟）→ 缓解（按路径混用一致性模型）。
why_en: Stale reads costing real money lead to strong consistency, whose availability and latency costs are contained by applying it only to critical paths.

scenario: 新服务预估 2 万 QPS（95% 是按主键的简单读）、200GB 数据，有人凭 2010 年的经验坚持必须先分片再加缓存。
scenario_en: A new service is projected at 20k QPS (95% simple primary-key reads) on 200GB, and someone citing 2010-era experience insists on sharding plus caching up front.
q: 脑子里装着 2010 年代的硬件数字做设计，会导致什么？
q_en: What happens if you design with outdated 2010s hardware numbers in mind?
options: 设计更保守更安全
过早提出分片和缓存，为还不存在的瓶颈加复杂度
没有影响
面试官会觉得你经验老到
options_en: The design becomes more conservative and safer.
You propose sharding and caching earlier than needed, adding complexity for a bottleneck that doesn't exist yet.
It has no effect.
The interviewer will think you're seasoned.
why: 今天的单机 NVMe、几十核、几百 GB 内存，配合索引良好的简单读，通常能扛几万 QPS（具体数要看 payload、查询复杂度、索引、缓存命中率和压测方法）。用十几年前的硬件印象估算，会在远未到瓶颈时就提出分片和缓存。
why_en: A modern box with NVMe, dozens of cores, and hundreds of GB of RAM can often serve tens of thousands of QPS of well-indexed simple reads (the exact figure depends on payload, query complexity, indexes, cache hit rate, and benchmark method). Estimating with decade-old hardware intuition makes you propose sharding and caching long before the bottleneck exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统每秒处理的查询数，常用来估算需要多少台服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is the number of queries a system handles per second, often used to estimate how many servers you need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

对，现代硬件比老数字强得多，用旧认知就会为不存在的瓶颈提前加复杂度。
用错年代的硬件数字直接决定了你在哪个负载点开始提分片，影响很实在。

Right — modern hardware is far stronger than those old numbers suggest, so outdated assumptions trigger sharding and caching too soon.

q: 补全延迟阶梯（影响几乎所有设计决策）：
q_en: Fill in the latency ladder that shapes almost every design decision.
text: 内存访问约 {{纳秒}} 级（~100 ns）；SSD 随机读约 {{微秒}} 级（几十到一百多 µs）；同数据中心一次网络往返约 {{亚毫秒}}（~0.5 ms）；跨大洲往返要几十到上百毫秒。
why: 每一级大约差两三个数量级：内存比 SSD 快约 1000 倍，SSD 读又比一次机房内往返快约 5-10 倍，机房内往返比跨大洲快约 100 倍。「要不要加缓存」「值不值得多地域部署」的判断都来自这些量级差。具体数字随硬件代际变化，记量级不记精确值。
why_en: Each rung is roughly two to three orders of magnitude apart: memory is ~1000× faster than SSD, an SSD read is ~5-10× faster than a same-DC round trip, and a same-DC round trip is ~100× faster than crossing a continent. Cache and multi-region decisions come from these gaps. Exact numbers shift with hardware generations, so remember orders of magnitude.
tradeoff: 本地内存访问延迟 vs 跨大洲网络调用延迟
scenario: 做设计决策（要不要加缓存、要不要多地域部署）前，先在脑子里过一遍延迟阶梯。
scenario_en: Before making design calls (add a cache? go multi-region?), run through the latency ladder in your head.
text_en: Memory access is on the order of {{nanoseconds}} (~100 ns); an SSD random read is {{microseconds}} (tens to ~150 µs); a same-datacenter network round trip is {{sub-millisecond}} (~0.5 ms); a cross-continent round trip is tens to hundreds of milliseconds.

scenario: 数据量还在增长，目前 500GB；写入量低、读副本够用、备份恢复时间可接受，团队在纠结现在是否该因为「存储量」把 Postgres 拆分片。
scenario_en: Data keeps growing and is now 500GB; write load is low, read replicas keep up, and backup/restore time is acceptable. The team is debating whether storage volume alone justifies sharding Postgres now.
q: 单个 Postgres 实例大约能舒适地承载多少存储？什么量级才该考虑分片？
q_en: Roughly how much storage can one Postgres instance comfortably hold, and when should sharding enter the conversation?

只能存 10GB
到了 1TB 就必须立刻分片
存储无上限

Only 10GB.
Sharding becomes mandatory the moment you hit 1TB.
Storage has no upper limit.

But sharding also depends on write throughput, replication lag on a single primary, backup/restore time, and vacuum cost, any of which can force a split earlier.

1000 TPS 就必须分库
options_en: At most 100 TPS and 10GB of storage.
Simple reads can reach tens of thousands of TPS (rule-of-thumb); start doing the math when writes pass ~10k TPS or uncached read latency climbs.
Unlimited TPS.
You must shard at 1000 TPS.
why: 这是经验锚点而不是规格：调优过的单库在简单索引查询下，读常能到几万 TPS、写到一万左右；具体数取决于 CPU/磁盘、payload、索引、事务与 fsync 配置、并发和压测方法。触发信号看趋势：写吞吐逼近实测上限、未命中读延迟上升、需要地域分布。
why_en: This is a rule-of-thumb anchor, not a spec: a tuned single instance with simple indexed queries often reaches tens of thousands of read TPS and around ten thousand writes; the real figure depends on CPU/disk, payload, indexes, transaction and fsync settings, concurrency, and benchmark method. Watch trends: writes nearing the measured ceiling, rising uncached read latency, or a need for geographic distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库每秒能处理的事务数，是判断单库还能不能扛的核心指标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS is the number of transactions a database can process per second, a key signal for whether a single instance can still keep up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储容量单位，1 TiB ≈ 1024 GB，用来衡量单库存储上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB (tebibyte) is a storage unit of about 1024 GB, used to gauge a single database's storage ceiling.

optionExplanations: 100 TPS 严重低估了现代调优过的数据库实力，会让人过早焦虑扩容。
对，这是经验锚点：调优过的单库简单读可到几万 TPS，真正该看的信号是写吞吐逼近上限或未命中读延迟上升。
硬件、连接数、锁竞争都有真实上限，不存在无限吞吐这回事。
1000 TPS 离单库真实上限还差得远，这个门槛定得太低了。
optionExplanations_en: One hundred TPS badly underestimates a modern tuned database, and it triggers scaling worries far too early.

Right — it is a rule-of-thumb anchor: a tuned single instance can reach tens of thousands of simple-read TPS, and the signals to watch are write throughput nearing the ceiling or rising uncached read latency.
Hardware, connection limits, and lock contention all cap throughput; there's no such thing as unlimited TPS.
One thousand TPS is still well below a single instance's real ceiling, so that threshold is set far too low.

scenario: 线上 Redis 集群做容量规划，负载以小 value 的简单 GET/SET 为主；要知道单节点大致量级，以及什么信号说明该扩容或优化。
scenario_en: You are capacity-planning a Redis cluster serving mostly small-value GET/SET; you need rough per-node anchors and signals for expansion or optimization.
q: 缓存（Redis 级别）的关键量级与告警触发点是？
q_en: What Redis-scale cache anchors and alert triggers should you remember?
options: 延迟 100ms、1k ops/s
延迟 1 秒、10k ops/s
客户端视角约 1ms、单节点 10万+ ops/s；命中率持续下滑或内存逼近 maxmemory 时扩容/优化
没有任何上限
options_en: 100ms latency, 1k ops per second.
1 second latency, 10k ops per second.
About 1ms client-side, 100k+ ops/s per node; scale or optimize when hit rate keeps falling or memory nears maxmemory.
No upper limit at all.
why: 简单命令下 Redis 单节点常见 10 万以上 ops/s、客户端延迟约 1ms（服务端处理多为亚毫秒）；大 value、Lua、大 ZSET、网络带宽会显著拉低。单节点内存一般保持在几十 GB 量级，大数据量靠集群分片而不是把单节点做到 TB。扩容信号看趋势：命中率持续下滑、内存逼近 maxmemory 并开始驱逐、延迟上升；具体阈值按业务定。
why_en: With simple commands, a Redis node commonly does 100k+ ops/s at about 1ms client-side latency (server-side is usually sub-millisecond); large values, Lua, big ZSETs, and network bandwidth lower that sharply. Keep per-node memory in the tens of GB and scale data via cluster sharding rather than TB-sized nodes. Scale-up signals are trends: falling hit rate, memory nearing maxmemory with evictions, rising latency; exact thresholds depend on the workload.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

optionExplanations: 100ms、1k ops/s 完全低估了内存型缓存的真实速度，会误导容量判断。
1 秒延迟更是离谱地慢，Redis 这类内存缓存不会是这个数量级。
对，简单命令下 Redis 单节点常见客户端约 1ms、10 万+ ops/s；命中率持续下滑或内存逼近 maxmemory 才是该扩容的信号。
内存容量和单机网络吞吐都有硬上限，不存在完全无上限的缓存节点。
optionExplanations_en: 100ms latency and 1k ops per second badly underestimate an in-memory cache's real speed, which would mislead capacity planning.
One second of latency is even more implausible — an in-memory cache like Redis never runs that slow.
Right — with simple commands a single Redis node typically runs about 1ms client-side and 100k+ ops/s; a steadily falling hit rate or memory nearing maxmemory is the real scale-up signal.
Memory capacity and single-node network throughput both have hard ceilings; no cache node is truly limitless.

scenario: 你在为 Kafka 集群做容量规划，消息约几百字节、开启批量发送和压缩；要知道单 broker 大致量级和扩容信号。
scenario_en: You are capacity-planning a Kafka cluster with messages of a few hundred bytes, batching and compression enabled; you need rough per-broker anchors and expansion signals.
q: 消息队列的关键量级是？
q_en: What message-queue scale anchors should you remember?
options: 每 broker 每秒 100 条
每秒 1 万条是极限
端到端延迟至少 1 秒
单 broker 可到几十万到约百万条/秒；接近实测上限或 consumer lag 持续增长时扩容
options_en: One hundred messages per second per broker.
Ten thousand per second is the ceiling.
At least one second of end-to-end latency.
A single broker can reach hundreds of thousands to about a million messages per second; scale when nearing the measured ceiling or consumer lag keeps growing.
why: 这是 Kafka 在小消息、批量、压缩条件下的经验量级；实际吞吐受消息大小、网卡/磁盘带宽、acks 与副本数、分区数影响，追求极致吞吐时端到端延迟也会变高。真正要盯的是接近压测上限、热点分区和持续增长的 consumer lag。其它 MQ（如 RabbitMQ、SQS）量级不同，不能套用。
why_en: This is a Kafka rule-of-thumb for small, batched, compressed messages; real throughput depends on message size, NIC/disk bandwidth, acks and replication factor, and partition count, and pushing throughput raises end-to-end latency. Watch for nearing the benchmarked ceiling, hot partitions, and growing consumer lag. Other MQs such as RabbitMQ or SQS have different profiles.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者处理进度落后于消息队列写入进度的差值，持续增长说明消费能力跟不上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consumer lag is how far a consumer's processing position trails the queue's write position; a growing lag means consumers can't keep up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息队列里把一个 topic 拆成的并行处理单元数量，决定了消费并行度的上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partition count is how many parallel units a topic is split into, capping how much consumer parallelism is possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息队列集群里实际存储和转发消息的服务器节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a server node in a message-queue cluster that actually stores and forwards messages.

optionExplanations: 每秒 100 条严重低估了消息队列的真实吞吐能力，实际数量级要高得多。
1 万条/秒还远没到单 broker 的真实极限，把这个当上限会过早喊扩容。
健康的消息队列端到端延迟通常在个位数毫秒，1 秒是不正常的慢。
对，小消息、批量、压缩下单 broker 可到几十万到约百万条/秒，该盯的信号是接近实测上限或 consumer lag 持续增长。
optionExplanations_en: One hundred messages per second badly underestimates a message queue's real throughput, which runs orders of magnitude higher.
Ten thousand per second is still far short of a single broker's real ceiling; treating it as the limit triggers scaling far too early.
A healthy queue's end-to-end latency usually sits in single-digit milliseconds; one second would be abnormally slow.

Right — with small, batched, compressed messages a single broker can reach hundreds of thousands to about a million messages per second; the signals are nearing the measured ceiling or growing consumer lag.

scenario: 面试刚开场，你还在澄清需求，面试官没有要求估算，你却想先把 QPS、存储、服务器台数一次算清楚，给整个设计打地基。
scenario_en: The interview just opened and you're still clarifying requirements; the interviewer hasn't asked for estimates, yet you feel the urge to crunch QPS, storage, and server counts up front.
q: back-of-the-envelope 估算应该在什么时候做？
q_en: When should you do back-of-the-envelope estimation?
options: 开场就一次性把 QPS、存储、每秒写入和服务器台数全部算完，当作后续设计的地基
等某个决策要用到数字时才算，比如该不该分片、单 Redis 够不够
系统设计全程都不用估算，凭经验直接拍板选型就行
只在面试官明确说『帮我估一下容量』时才动手，平时一律不主动算
options_en: Crunch QPS, storage, write rate, and server count all at once up front as the foundation for the whole design.
Only when a decision needs the numbers, e.g. whether to shard or whether one Redis is enough.
You never need to estimate in system design; just pick designs from experience.
Only when the interviewer explicitly says 'estimate the capacity for me,' otherwise never volunteer it.
why: Back-of-the-envelope 估算是决策工具：在遇到岔路（要不要分片、一个 Redis 够不够）时才算，用数字支撑那一步选择。开场把所有数字算一遍，大部分不会挂到任何决策上，还挤掉架构讨论时间。如果面试官主动要求估算，就照做。
why_en: Back-of-the-envelope math is a decision tool: do it at forks like whether to shard or whether one Redis suffices, so the numbers back that choice. Crunching everything up front produces numbers tied to no decision and eats architecture time. If the interviewer asks for estimates, do them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用粗略数量级心算来做容量判断的方法，也叫 back-of-the-envelope。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Back-of-the-envelope estimation is doing rough order-of-magnitude math in your head to make a capacity decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量系统读写请求速率的常用指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is queries per second, a common measure of a system's request rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存键值存储，常被当作缓存来挡住数据库读压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache in front of the database.

optionExplanations: 开场把所有数字一次算完，大部分挂不到任何决策上，只是空转，还挤掉架构讨论的时间。
对：估算服务于具体决策，遇到分片或缓存容量这类岔路时才算，数字才有落点。
凭感觉拍板会在被追问『多少台、扛不扛得住』时露怯，估算正是用来回答这类追问的。
被动等指令太保守：这些容量决策该由你主动用数字支撑，不必等面试官开口。
optionExplanations_en: Crunching every number at the start leaves most of them tied to no decision — busywork that also eats architecture time.
Right: estimation serves a specific decision, done at forks like sharding or cache sizing so the numbers land.
Gut calls fall apart under 'how many servers, will it hold?'; estimation is exactly what answers those probes.
Waiting to be told is too passive: you should volunteer the numbers that back these capacity calls.

scenario: 面试官问『这个服务大概需要多少台应用服务器』。预期峰值 5 万 rps，实测单台机器约能扛 5K rps。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how many app servers the service needs. Peak is about 50K requests per second, and one machine handles roughly 5K per second.
q: 当场该怎么估出台数？
q_en: How do you estimate the server count on the spot?
options: 总 rps ÷ 单机 rps ≈ 10 台，再加余量（headroom）
干脆上 5 万台，一个请求配一台服务器最稳妥，不用估
服务器台数和 rps 无关，只看数据总量有多少 TB 来决定
得先部署 1 台压测到彻底崩溃、再做线性外推，面试现场其实根本没法当场给出准确台数
options_en: Total rps ÷ per-machine rps ≈ 10 servers, then add headroom.
Just spin up 50K machines — one server per request is safest, no estimate needed.
Server count has nothing to do with rps; decide it purely from how many TB of data you hold.
You'd have to deploy one box, stress it to full collapse, then extrapolate linearly — you really can't give an accurate count live.
why: 公式：台数 = 总 rps ÷ 单机 rps；rps 是 requests per second（每秒请求数），5 万 ÷ 5K ≈ 10 台，再加 20-30% 余量抗峰值和单机故障。这个数是后续算成本和负载均衡后端池大小的基数。
why_en: Formula: servers = total rps divided by per-machine rps; rps is requests per second, so 50K over 5K is about 10, plus 20 to 30 percent headroom for spikes and failures, and that count sizes cost and the load-balancer pool.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量服务承受的请求速率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: rps is requests per second, the rate of requests a service takes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在算出的基线之外预留的余量，用来吸收流量峰值和单机故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Headroom is spare capacity kept beyond the baseline to absorb traffic spikes and machine failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 太字节，衡量存储容量的单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TB is terabyte, a unit of storage capacity.

optionExplanations: 对：先做除法得基线台数，再留余量吸收峰值和单机故障——这就是面试官想看的演算。
一台配一个请求是把并发误当成总量；单机每秒能处理数千请求，不是只服务一个。
TB 决定的是要不要分片存储，不决定无状态应用服务器台数，这里混了两个轴。
文章要的正是当场走一遍除法；说估不出来等于回避了这道能力题。
optionExplanations_en: Right: divide for a baseline count, then keep headroom for spikes and failures — the math they want to see.
One server per request confuses concurrency with total volume; a box serves thousands per second, not one.
TB drives whether to shard storage, not stateless app-server count — this mixes two different axes.
The article wants you to walk the division live; saying it can't be done dodges the very skill being tested.

scenario: 团队想把内部用的 gRPC 服务直接开放给浏览器前端调用，省掉再写一层 REST。
scenario_en: A team wants to expose their internal gRPC service directly to browser front-ends to skip writing a REST layer.
q: 直接把 gRPC 暴露给浏览器会怎样？
q_en: What happens if you expose gRPC directly to browsers?
options: 浏览器不原生支持 gRPC；用 gRPC-Web 还得架代理转译且特性不全
完全没问题，gRPC 本来就是为浏览器直连设计的
能用，只是 JSON 会比 protobuf 慢一点而已
浏览器会自动把 gRPC 降级成普通的 HTTP/1.1 请求，功能和性能都不受影响
options_en: Browsers don't natively support gRPC; gRPC-Web needs a translating proxy and still lacks some features.
No problem at all — gRPC was designed for browsers to call directly.
It works; JSON is just a bit slower than protobuf, that's all.
The browser auto-downgrades gRPC to a plain HTTP/1.1 request, with no loss of function or performance.
why: 浏览器的 fetch/XHR 发不出 gRPC 的 HTTP/2 二进制帧，直连时前端请求直接失败；gRPC-Web 能补但要额外架一层代理转译、且不支持全部 gRPC 特性。所以对外用 REST、对内才用 gRPC。
why_en: A browser's fetch and XHR can't emit gRPC's HTTP/2 binary frames, so a direct call just fails; gRPC-Web patches it but needs an extra translating proxy and drops some gRPC features, which is why you use REST externally and gRPC only internally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化的高性能远程调用框架，多用于服务间通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a high-performance remote-call framework over HTTP/2 with binary serialization, mostly used service-to-service.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器间接调用 gRPC 的方案，需要一层代理把请求翻译成浏览器能发的格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC-Web lets browsers reach gRPC indirectly through a proxy that translates requests into a browser-sendable form.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 的第二版，在一条连接上多路复用请求并用二进制帧传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the second version of HTTP, multiplexing requests over one connection using binary frames.

termDefinitions.meaning: Protocol Buffers，一种紧凑的二进制序列化格式，gRPC 默认用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Protobuf is Protocol Buffers, a compact binary serialization format that gRPC uses by default.

optionExplanations: 对：浏览器发不出 gRPC 帧，硬要用得靠 gRPC-Web 代理，还会丢掉流式等特性。
gRPC 是为服务间高性能通信设计的，从来不是给浏览器直连用的。
问题不在 JSON 还是 protobuf 谁快，而在浏览器根本发不出这种请求。
没有自动降级这回事；浏览器不认 gRPC，不会魔法般转成 HTTP/1.1。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a browser can't emit gRPC frames, so you'd need a gRPC-Web proxy and still lose streaming and other features.
gRPC targets high-performance service-to-service calls; it was never meant for direct browser use.
The issue isn't JSON-vs-protobuf speed — the browser simply can't send the request at all.
There's no auto-downgrade; the browser doesn't understand gRPC and won't magically turn it into HTTP/1.1.

scenario: 全球用户拉取图片、JS 等静态资源，源站只在单一区域，跨洲用户加载明显偏慢。
scenario_en: Users worldwide fetch static assets like images and JS, but the origin sits in a single region, so cross-continent users load it noticeably slowly.
q: 怎么把静态资源的全球延迟降下来？
q_en: How do you cut the global latency of static assets?
options: 用 CDN，把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
给源站换更强的 CPU 和更大带宽
把源站服务器搬到离公司总部最近的机房
开启 gzip 压缩，把静态文件体积压得更小就能抵消跨洲物理距离
options_en: Use a CDN to cache static content on edge servers near users.
Give the origin a stronger CPU and more bandwidth.
Move the origin to the data center closest to company HQ.
Turn on gzip so smaller static files cancel out the cross-continent physical distance.
why: 跨洲往返有光速下限，处理再快也省不掉传播时间；CDN 把静态内容复制到靠近用户的边缘节点，请求就近命中，绕开物理距离。代价：多一层缓存要管失效，动态数据仍得回源。
why_en: Cross-continent round trips have a speed-of-light floor that faster processing can't remove, so a CDN caches static content on edge nodes near users to serve locally and dodge the distance.
whenOtherWins: 内容是高度个性化或强实时的动态数据、无法在边缘缓存时，CDN 帮不上，还是得靠区域部署或就近的动态源站。
tradeoff: CDN 就近分发的低延迟 vs 多一层边缘缓存的失效管理成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点、就近分发的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network that caches static content on edge servers close to users to serve it locally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布在各地、离用户很近的缓存服务器，用来就近响应请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge node is a geographically distributed cache server close to users that answers requests locally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种压缩算法，减小传输的字节数但不改变往返的传播时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gzip is a compression algorithm that shrinks transferred bytes but doesn't change round-trip propagation time.

optionExplanations: 对：把内容放到用户附近的边缘节点，用地理位置绕开跨洲物理延迟。
更强的 CPU/带宽只缩短服务端处理时间，改不了跨洲传播的物理下限。
搬到总部附近只对总部用户有利，对其他大洲用户反而可能更慢。
压缩减少的是字节数和轮次，单次跨洲往返的传播时间一点不减。
optionExplanations_en: Right: placing content on edge nodes near users uses geography to dodge cross-continent latency.
A faster CPU or more bandwidth only trims server processing, not the physical floor of cross-continent propagation.
Moving near HQ only helps HQ users and can be slower for users on other continents.
Compression cuts bytes and round trips, but a single cross-continent trip's propagation time is unchanged.

scenario: 面试要你为一个普通 CRUD 业务勾勒对外 API，没有实时推送或极端性能要求。
scenario_en: You're asked to sketch a public API for a routine CRUD service with no real-time push or extreme performance needs.
q: 90% 的面试里对外 API 该默认用什么风格？
q_en: For most interviews, what API style should a public API default to?
options: REST：资源映射到 URL，用 HTTP 方法操作
GraphQL，让客户端自定义每次查询返回哪些字段
gRPC，二进制协议对外性能最好
自己设计一套私有 RPC 协议，完全贴合业务语义、最灵活
options_en: REST: map resources to URLs and act on them with HTTP methods.
GraphQL, letting the client pick which fields each query returns.
gRPC, whose binary protocol is fastest for public APIs.
Design a private RPC protocol that fits the business exactly and is most flexible.
why: 对外 API 默认 REST：资源映射成 URL（/users/{id}）、用 HTTP 方法操作（POST /events/{id}/bookings），人人都懂、到处能跑。代价：复杂查询或极致性能时不如专用方案灵活。
why_en: Default a public API to REST, mapping resources to URLs like /users/{id} and acting via HTTP methods like POST /events/{id}/bookings, because it's universally understood and expected.
whenOtherWins: 客户端字段需求差异大、想在一次请求里精确取数减少往返时用 GraphQL；纯内部、性能关键的调用才用 gRPC。
tradeoff: 通用直白的 REST vs 更贴合特定需求但更重的 GraphQL/gRPC

termDefinitions.meaning: 把资源映射到 URL、用 HTTP 方法（GET/POST/…）操作的接口风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that maps resources to URLs and operates on them with HTTP methods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种查询语言，让客户端在一次请求里精确声明要哪些字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets the client declare exactly which fields a single request returns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化的高性能远程调用框架，多用于服务间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a high-performance remote-call framework over HTTP/2 with binary serialization, mainly service-to-service.

termDefinitions.meaning: 远程过程调用，像调用本地函数一样调用远端服务的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPC is remote procedure call, invoking a remote service's method as if it were a local function.

optionExplanations: 对：REST 资源+HTTP 方法的映射直白通用，是面试和生产的安全默认。
GraphQL 在客户端取数需求千差万别时才划算，普通 CRUD 上是过度设计。
gRPC 快但浏览器不原生支持，对外要架代理，通常只用在内部服务间。
私有协议最灵活也最难维护，别人接入要重学，普通业务不值得。
optionExplanations_en: Right: REST's resource-plus-HTTP-method mapping is plain and universal, the safe default in interviews and production.
GraphQL pays off only when clients have wildly varied field needs; on plain CRUD it's over-engineering.
gRPC is fast but browsers don't support it natively, so external use needs a proxy — keep it internal.
A private protocol is most flexible but hardest to maintain; every integrator relearns it, rarely worth it.

scenario: 缓存里存着用户资料。写库后必须保证下一次读就拿到新值——这是一条强新鲜度的读路径。
scenario_en: User profiles live in the cache. After a write, the very next read must return the new value — this read path demands strong freshness.
q: 对『必须立刻新鲜』的数据，该选哪种失效策略？
q_en: For data that must be immediately fresh, which invalidation strategy fits?
options: 写库后立即删除或更新缓存条目，下次读回源重建
只靠一个很长的 TTL，等它自然过期
干脆永久缓存、不设失效，靠重启清空
给所有缓存条目统一设成几小时 TTL，容忍这段窗口内的陈旧数据
options_en: On write, immediately delete or update the cache entry so the next read rebuilds from the source.
Rely on a single long TTL and let it expire on its own.
Cache forever with no invalidation and clear it only on restart.
Give every entry the same multi-hour TTL and tolerate stale data within that window.
why: 新鲜度要求决定失效策略：必须立刻读到新值就在写后立即失效缓存，下次读回源重建，不容忍陈旧窗口。代价：每次写都要多一次缓存删除/更新操作，逻辑更复杂。
why_en: Freshness sets the strategy: if the next read must see the new value, invalidate the cache right at write time so the next read rebuilds from source, accepting the extra write-path work.
whenOtherWins: 能容忍几秒到几分钟陈旧时，用短 TTL（或配合立即失效）更省事，不必让每次写都改动缓存。
tradeoff: 立即失效的强新鲜 vs 短 TTL 的实现简单但有陈旧窗口

termDefinitions.meaning: 在底层数据变化后，把缓存里的旧副本删掉或更新，避免读到陈旧数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidation is removing or updating a stale cached copy after the underlying data changes so reads don't see old values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后自动过期需要重新加载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is time to live, how long a cache entry survives before it expires and must be reloaded.

optionExplanations: 对：写后立即失效保证下一次读回源，没有陈旧窗口，代价是写路径多一步。
长 TTL 意味着写完后仍会读到旧值一直到过期，满足不了『立刻新鲜』。
永不失效会长期返回旧资料，改了头像也刷不掉，是最差的方案。
统一几小时 TTL 是拿新鲜度换省事，对这条强新鲜路径不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Right: invalidating on write forces the next read from source with no stale window, at the cost of one extra write step.
A long TTL keeps serving the old value after a write until it expires, so it can't be immediately fresh.
Never invalidating serves stale profiles indefinitely; a new avatar never shows up — the worst option.
A uniform multi-hour TTL trades freshness for ease, which doesn't hold on this strong-freshness path.

scenario: 一批 feature flag 和配置值：几乎从不变化，但每个请求都要读一次。
scenario_en: A set of feature flags and config values: they almost never change, yet every request reads them.
q: 这种小而极少变化的值，缓存在哪里最合适？
q_en: Where should you cache small, rarely changing values like these?
options: 放进程内内存缓存，读取零网络开销
放外部 Redis，和核心业务数据一样对待
放 CDN 边缘节点，让全球用户就近读取
每次都直接查数据库，反正配置读起来也不算慢
options_en: In an in-process memory cache, so reads have zero network cost.
In external Redis, treated like core business data.
On CDN edge nodes so users worldwide read it nearby.
Query the database every time, since config reads aren't that slow anyway.
why: 小、极少变化、每请求都读的值适合进程内缓存：直接读本地内存、零网络往返，最快最省。代价：无法跨实例同步，值更新要靠重启或 TTL，所以只适合能容忍短暂不一致的配置类数据。
why_en: Small, rarely changing, per-request values fit an in-process cache: reads hit local memory with zero network hop, at the cost of no cross-instance sync, so use it only for config-like data that tolerates brief inconsistency.
whenOtherWins: 值较大、变化频繁、或需要多实例立刻看到同一份最新值时，改用外部 Redis 统一管理。
tradeoff: 进程内缓存的零延迟零依赖 vs 无法跨实例同步、更新要等重启或 TTL

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据直接存在应用进程自身内存里的缓存，读取不走网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-process cache stores data in the application process's own memory, so reads avoid the network.

termDefinitions.meaning: 控制某功能开关的配置项，用于灰度或快速开关功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature flag is a config switch that turns a feature on or off, used for rollouts or quick toggles.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立进程的内存键值存储，常作为多实例共享的外部缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a standalone in-memory key-value store, commonly used as an external cache shared across instances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户边缘节点的分发网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on edge nodes close to users.

optionExplanations: 对：值小又几乎不变，放本地内存零网络开销，是这类数据的最优解。
外部 Redis 每次读都要一次网络往返，对小配置值属于杀鸡用牛刀。
CDN 是给静态资产就近分发的，不适合放应用逻辑要读的配置值。
每次查库徒增延迟和负载，配置这种极少变化的值缓存起来收益明显。
optionExplanations_en: Right: tiny and near-static, so local memory with no network hop is optimal for this data.
External Redis costs a network round trip per read — overkill for small config values.
CDNs distribute static assets nearby, not config values that application logic reads.
Hitting the DB every time adds latency and load; near-static config clearly benefits from caching.

scenario: 多租户 SaaS，每个公司（租户）只查询自己那部分数据，你在选分片方式。
scenario_en: A multi-tenant SaaS where each company (tenant) only ever queries its own data, and you're choosing a sharding scheme.
q: 什么情况下 range（范围）分片是合适的？
q_en: When is range-based sharding a good fit?
options: 访问模式天然按租户分区、各租户只读自己数据时
任何时候都行，range 分片的负载永远比 hash 更均匀
写入是单调递增的时间序列、最近数据被反复读写时
需要频繁做跨所有分片的全局聚合查询时
options_en: When access naturally partitions by tenant and each tenant only reads its own data.
Always — range sharding's load is always more even than hash.
When writes are a monotonically increasing time series and recent data is read and written repeatedly.
When you frequently run global aggregations across all shards.
why: range 分片在访问天然分区时才安全：多租户 SaaS 每个租户只碰自己那段范围，查询命中单一分片、彼此隔离。代价：一旦某个范围变热（如最新时间段），负载就会挤到一个分片上，这时该改用 hash 分片打散。
why_en: Range sharding is safe only when access naturally partitions: in multi-tenant SaaS each tenant touches just its own range, so queries hit one isolated shard, at the risk that a hot range piles load on a single shard.
whenOtherWins: 访问不天然分区、或某个范围会成为热点（如单调递增的时间序列）时，改用 hash 分片把负载均匀打散。
tradeoff: range 分片对天然分区数据的隔离与局部性 vs 范围过热时的热点风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 按分片键的取值范围切数据，同一范围落在同一分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range sharding splits data by ranges of the shard key, so one range lives on one shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对分片键哈希再取模选分片，数据分布均匀、天然防热点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash sharding hashes the shard key and takes a modulo to pick a shard, spreading data evenly to avoid hot spots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一套系统服务多个客户（租户），各租户数据彼此隔离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-tenant SaaS serves many customers (tenants) from one system, keeping each tenant's data isolated.

optionExplanations: 对：租户各查各的范围，查询落单分片又相互隔离，正是 range 分片的甜点。
range 并不天然更均匀——范围过热时它比 hash 更容易局部过载。
单调递增时间序列会把最新写入全挤到一个分片，正是 range 的热点雷区。
跨所有分片的全局聚合和分片键无关，range 帮不上，反而要扫全部分片。
optionExplanations_en: Right: each tenant queries its own range, hitting one isolated shard — the sweet spot for range sharding.
Range isn't inherently more even; when a range runs hot it overloads locally more than hash does.
A monotonic time series funnels the newest writes onto one shard — exactly range sharding's hot-spot trap.
Global aggregation across all shards is independent of the shard key; range doesn't help and must scan every shard.

scenario: 线上 Redis 命中率从平时的 95% 掉到 75%，内存用到 maxmemory 的 82% 且持续上涨，监控显示 evicted_keys 激增、key 频繁换进换出（cache churn）。
scenario_en: In production, Redis hit rate has fallen from its usual 95% to 75%, memory is at 82% of maxmemory and climbing, and evicted_keys is spiking as keys churn in and out.
q: 这几个信号一起出现意味着什么、该做什么？
q_en: What do these signals together mean, and what should you do?
options: 缓存已到扩容/优化临界：扩内存或加节点，并复查缓存了什么
只是正常波动，命中率和内存用量都不用管
说明该把缓存整个下线，让请求全部直接回源数据库
把 TTL 调到无限长就能把命中率拉回 100%，从此不必扩容
options_en: The cache is at its scale/optimize threshold: add memory or nodes and review what's cached.
Just normal fluctuation — neither hit rate nor memory needs attention.
It means take the cache fully offline and send every request straight to the database.
Set TTL to infinite to push hit rate back to 100% and never scale again.
why: 命中率相对基线明显下滑、内存逼近 maxmemory、evictions 激增，说明热点集装不下：条目被挤出又被重取，压力回落到数据库。动作是扩内存或加节点，并复查是否缓存了不该缓存的数据（冷数据、过大的 value）。80% 这类阈值是经验告警线，实际按业务基线定。
why_en: A clear drop from baseline hit rate, memory nearing maxmemory, and spiking evictions mean the hot set no longer fits: entries are evicted and refetched, pushing load back onto the database. Add memory or nodes and review what is cached (cold data, oversized values). Thresholds like 80% are rule-of-thumb alerts; set them from your own baseline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读请求在缓存中直接命中的比例，越高越少回源数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is the share of read requests served directly from cache; higher means fewer database fallbacks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目被频繁驱逐又重新加载的抖动，通常因内存装不下热点集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache churn is entries being repeatedly evicted and reloaded, usually because memory can't hold the hot set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存键值存储，常作为缓存挡在数据库前面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache in front of the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期自动过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is time to live, how long a cache entry lives before it expires.

optionExplanations: 对：三个信号同时出现正是扩容/优化临界，扩内存或加节点并复查缓存内容。
命中率跌破 80%、内存逼近满不是波动，是数据库即将被回源压力打到的前兆。
下线缓存会把全部读打到数据库，正好放大问题而不是解决它。
无限 TTL 不解决内存不够，反而让旧数据永不刷新、内存更快被撑爆。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the three signals together mark the scale/optimize threshold — add memory or nodes and review what's cached.
Hit rate under 80% with memory near full isn't fluctuation; it foreshadows the database taking the fallback load.
Taking the cache offline sends all reads to the database, amplifying the problem instead of fixing it.
Infinite TTL doesn't fix insufficient memory; it keeps stale data forever and fills memory faster.

scenario: 无状态应用服务器集群：CPU 稳定在 75%、P99 响应开始超出 SLA，单机连接数逼近本系统实测的 10 万上限；下游数据库和缓存延迟都正常。
scenario_en: A stateless app-server fleet: CPU sits steadily at 75%, P99 latency starts breaching the SLA, and per-instance connections approach this system's measured 100K ceiling; downstream database and cache latency are normal.
q: 这几个信号一起出现意味着什么？
q_en: What do these signals together mean?
options: 已达扩容触发点，应水平加机器分摊负载
只要还没到 100% CPU 就绝对安全，什么都不用做
换更大内存的机器就能同时解决 CPU 和连接数问题
把 SLA 目标放宽一点，让超标的响应看起来重新达标就行
options_en: It's the scale-out trigger: add machines horizontally to spread the load.
As long as CPU isn't at 100% it's perfectly safe; do nothing.
A machine with more memory would fix both CPU and connection-count problems.
Just relax the SLA target so the breaching latency looks compliant again.
why: 下游正常、三项指标都在应用层越线，说明单机吃紧。应用服务器无状态，水平加机器最直接；台数按「CPU 和连接两个维度分别算，取较大值，再留余量」。垂直扩容（更多核）也能缓解 CPU，但连接上限和单点风险仍在，所以首选水平扩容。
why_en: With downstream healthy and all three signals crossing in the app tier, the instances are saturated. The servers are stateless, so scaling out is the most direct fix; size it by computing count from both CPU and connections, taking the larger, plus headroom. Scaling up with more cores could ease CPU, but the connection ceiling and single-box risk remain, so scale-out is preferred.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议，对外承诺的性能/可用性目标，如 P99 延迟上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is a service-level agreement, the promised performance or availability target such as a P99 latency ceiling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟，99% 的请求比它快，用来衡量尾部延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 is the 99th-percentile latency: 99% of requests are faster, used to gauge tail latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过增加机器数量分摊负载，而不是把单机换得更强。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling spreads load by adding more machines rather than making one machine bigger.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器，其利用率反映计算资源的繁忙程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CPU is the central processing unit; its utilization reflects how busy compute resources are.

optionExplanations: 对：三个信号同时越线正是水平扩容的触发点，加机器分摊负载。
不到 100% 不等于安全——CPU 70%+ 且响应超 SLA 时用户已经在受影响。
换大内存机器治不了 CPU 瓶颈，也拉不高单机连接上限，是找错了轴。
放宽 SLA 只是改指标掩盖问题，用户体验和真实延迟一点没变好。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the three signals crossing together is the scale-out trigger — add machines to spread load.
Under 100% isn't safe; at 70%+ CPU with latency past SLA, users are already affected.
A bigger-memory box doesn't cure a CPU bottleneck or raise the connection ceiling — wrong axis.
Relaxing the SLA just repaints the metric to hide the problem; real latency and UX are unchanged.
